questions.stem: A file has NTFS permissions of Full Control for a user, but the Share permission for that user is Read. What access does the user get when connecting over the network?

choices.text: Read, because the most restrictive of NTFS and Share wins
Full Control, because NTFS always wins
Modify, the average of the two

questions.explanation: When combining NTFS and Share permissions over the network, the most restrictive permission wins. Read is more restrictive than Full Control, so the user gets Read.
questions.trap: NTFS does not 'always win'; over the network the effective permission is the more restrictive of the two sets.

questions.stem: A folder inherits Read from its parent, but an administrator sets an explicit Deny on a specific file inside it for one user. What is the effective result for that user on that file?

choices.text: The inherited permission always overrides explicit settings
The explicit permission on the file overrides the inherited one
Permissions cannot be set at the file level, only the folder level
Both are ignored and the user gets Full Control

questions.explanation: An explicit permission set directly on a file overrides an inherited permission from the parent folder.
questions.trap: Inheritance flows parent-to-child, but an explicit setting on the object takes precedence over what it inherited.

questions.stem: A standard user tries to install software and is prompted for administrator credentials before the system change is allowed. Which Windows feature is doing this?
questions.explanation: UAC is the gatekeeper that stops a system-wide change and asks for admin credentials before allowing it.
questions.trap: Windows Hello is a sign-in method (PIN/face/fingerprint), not the elevation prompt for system changes.

questions.stem: Which built-in Windows tool encrypts an entire OS volume so the data is unreadable if the drive is stolen, and has a 'To Go' variant for removable USB drives?
questions.explanation: BitLocker provides full-disk encryption of the OS volume; BitLocker To Go extends that protection to removable USB drives.
questions.trap: EFS encrypts individual files and folders tied to a user account, not the whole volume.

questions.stem: A user wants to encrypt just a few sensitive files and folders, tied to their own user-account credentials, without encrypting the whole disk. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: EFS encrypts individual files and folders, tying them to the user's account credentials - the granular option.
questions.trap: BitLocker (and To Go) does whole-volume encryption, which is more than 'just a few files'.

questions.stem: In Active Directory, what is the purpose of an Organizational Unit (OU)?

choices.text: It encrypts the domain controller's disk
It groups users and computers (like departments) so Group Policy can be applied to them
It replaces the need for a domain controller
It is the antivirus engine for the domain

questions.explanation: OUs group users and computers - like departments in a building - so Group Policy can be applied to those groupings.
questions.trap: OUs organize objects for policy; they don't encrypt anything or replace the domain controller.

questions.stem: An admin changes a Group Policy and wants it applied to a machine immediately rather than waiting for the next refresh. Which command is used?
questions.explanation: gpupdate /force forces Group Policy to apply immediately.
questions.trap: sfc /scannow repairs system files; it has nothing to do with Group Policy refresh.

questions.stem: Which Group Policy capability automatically copies a user's Desktop and Documents to a server so they follow the user and are backed up?
questions.explanation: Folder redirection (applied via Group Policy) points a user's Desktop/Documents to a server location, which also backs them up centrally.
questions.trap: BitLocker To Go encrypts removable drives; it does not redirect user folders to a server.

questions.stem: Best practice is to do daily work in which account type, elevating only when necessary?
questions.explanation: You should perform daily work in a standard account and only elevate privileges when an admin task requires it.
questions.trap: Running day-to-day in the Administrator account is exactly what the best practice warns against.

questions.stem: Which statement about keeping Microsoft Defender Antivirus effective is correct?

choices.text: It only works if BitLocker is enabled
Its virus definitions/signatures must be kept updated to catch the latest threats
It must be disabled before joining a domain
It replaces the need for a firewall

questions.explanation: Defender's real-time protection relies on up-to-date virus definitions (signatures) to recognize the latest threats.
questions.trap: Antivirus and the firewall are complementary; Defender does not remove the need for a firewall.
